question: How did astronomers weigh the black hole at the centre of the Milky Way without ever seeing it?
answer: By timing the stars around it. One star, S2, loops round an empty point every 16 years, passing within about 120 times the Earth–Sun distance at some 7,650 km/s. Only about four million suns' worth of mass, packed into a dark speck, can swing a star that hard.
move: When the thing itself hides, measure what it does to its neighbours.
ask: Whose influence in my life can I only see in how the people around them behave?
